event: At dawn a gauntleted hand knocks three measured times on the warehouse's loading door.
Callum has been up an hour: overnight Essence hit 8,600, up from 8,200 the day before.
Mira, on perimeter patrol since 4 AM, reports four Vanguard heavies and a sergeant in full gear.
He slides his field notebook under the cot's mattress, not because anything in it is illegal.
Jin, who moved in two days ago over a leaking roof, surfaces from his hoodie and goes pale.
Should he pull his summons from the Shardfield? Leave them running, Callum says; they hide nothing.
"We're a little bit hiding something," Jin says, very quietly. Callum opens the door.
Sergeant Tomas Bray, in Guardian plate, about Level 35, with four soldiers of Level 25 or more.
He hands over Compact Security Directive 4-17: an inspection of all construct operations.
The authority is a Resource Security Council likely a week old; four armed soldiers make it moot.
Bray sweeps the room, and his jaw tightens at the Enhancement Construct's tight feedback spiral.
Four constructs: combat, gathering, processing and feedback. "Standard," Bray repeats.
He knows Mira: "Vasquez. Didn't expect to see you here." "Morning, Sergeant."
"I'm standing in this warehouse. You can draw your own conclusions." Bray recalculates.
For ninety minutes Bray asks precise, competent questions about Flux draw and thread timing.
He lingers at the Enhancement Construct; Callum explains it simply and leaves out the growth curve.
Quietly: "You're generating more than a ten-man farming squad. The Commander noticed."
Then officially: every loop must pause for a safety verification. About fourteen hours.
His +31% Compound Growth will reset to zero: about forty-five hours of output lost.
His face shows nothing. "Understood. I'll initiate construct standby."
Sentinel, Collector, Refinery, and last the Enhancement Construct, its spiral unwinding to dust.
Compound loop suspended, no constructs active, +31% lost. The warehouse goes quiet.
For two hours the squad catalogs everything; a crossbowman scans the Sentinel with a Vanguard tool.
Jin sits rigid on his cot, Pixel curled at his ankle, answering in clipped, accurate sentences.
Bray reads the new rule: unaffiliated construct operators must register and face quarterly audits.
And pay a further ten percent Residuum contribution, on top of the existing surcharge.
Refuse, and their constructs lose access to the Overgrowth and the Rustbelt Flats.
Without those zones the loop starves. Drake Morrison understands systems.
"Thank you, Sergeant." Something like recognition moves behind Bray's eyes.
Fourteen days to register; he'd recommend sooner. The door shuts like a period.
Mira lets go of her pommel one finger at a time and paces: "That was not an inspection."
It's Drake's boot on his neck, asking him to say thank you: a shakedown with a Compact seal.
Drake is scared of a Level 19 construct operator, she says, because his system scales.
Drake once offered her protection too; with people like that there's always an "or else."
She sees his thumb dimple the form and his careful breathing: not cold, but disciplined.
They won't take this from him, she thinks, and she stands between him and the door.
Jin paces: thirty-one percent gone, and a ten percent tax on whatever they rebuild.
"This isn't fair. We built it legally, and they turned it off because it works too well."
Systems work as their controllers say, Callum says: Drake isn't breaking rules, he's making them.
He smooths the form flat, takes his notebook from under the mattress, and opens a fresh page.
He writes the cost: fourteen hours down, Compound Growth from +31% to 0, about 45 hours lost.
Night: dead constructs, the Essence Ley's hum, fifteen unspent skill points burning.
Constructs are hostages in known places; he needs something that lives inside the System itself.
Two points raise Compile Familiar to 2: Pip sharpens, and chimes for the first time.
"Can you understand me?" A low, steady chime: yes. A loneliness he'd stopped noticing loosens.
Four points take Loop Analysis to 7: he can now see System processes and external monitoring.
He finds a cold Vanguard scan thread left on his Grinder's anchor, still watching.
Six points take Script Engine from 2 to 5: twenty lines, loops, functions, enemy detection.
Twelve points spent, three left. He begins writing scripts in the System, not his notebook.
The Grinder's new script adapts to enemy types, and moves off if a monitoring signature comes near.
The Collector reroutes around restricted zones; the Enhancement Construct tunes itself.
In the third hour, level up: 19 to 20, and a Loopweaver milestone adds one to every stat.

event: Intelligence 66, Wisdom 69, Idle Yield 2.40x: five levels from Condense, two weeks by projection.
Around midnight Mira brings two tin cups of instant coffee so bad it is nearly a debuff.
"You've got a plan." The beginning of one: no punching Bray, but Drake made uncomfortable.
The constructs were always the weakness; the answer is smarter ones that expect interference.
Pip chimes, and Mira blinks. Pip is a Substrate process, he says: no zone or catalog can touch it.
She expected more reaction; the new scripts will recover faster than the first build did.
Drake controls the zones, so he'll build something that needs none. Five more levels, then Condense.
He'll register and pay; by the time it matters, the audits will track a Level 1 with a 1.5x.
Mira laughs: let them build a file, then reset the equation. "They can't reset the architecture."
He writes his first real function: shift routes if watched, fall back, else stand by and log.
He gives the restart: the Enhancement Construct stirs first, then the Refinery, the Grinder last.
Compound Growth sits at 0%, and a single point of Essence ticks into his report.
The Commander noticed. Good. He is just getting started.
